memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said to Moses, 'Take fragrant spices — gum resin, onycha and galbanum — and pure frankincense, all in equal amounts, and make a fragrant blend of incense, the work of a perfumer. It is to be salted and pure and sacred. Grind some of it to powder and place it in front of the ark of the covenant law in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with you. It shall be most holy to you. Do not make any incense with this formula for yourselves; consider it holy to the Lord. Whoever makes incense like it to enjoy its fragrance must be cut off from their people.'" - Exodus 30:34-38 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes with the incense formula, and the same restriction applies: do not make this for yourselves. The phrase is pointed — no one was to reproduce it "to enjoy its fragrance." Something reserved for God was not to be taken for personal pleasure.

This gets at a real temptation. We can take what belongs to God and quietly repurpose it for ourselves — using spiritual gifts to build our own reputation, using ministry to meet our need for significance, using the name of God to advance our own agenda. The ingredients are holy; the use has become self-serving.

God's jealousy here is not petty. He is protecting the distinction between worship and self-interest, which we blur so easily. Jesus warned against practising righteousness to be seen by others (Matt 6:1). Ask honestly: is there something in my spiritual life that I have quietly turned toward my own benefit? What is holy to the Lord is meant to stay that way — offered up, not taken for personal enjoyment or advantage.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Have I repurposed something meant for God toward my own benefit or reputation?
What in my spiritual life needs to be handed back to God alone?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep me from taking what belongs to You and turning it toward myself. Purify my motives, and let what is holy to You remain wholly Yours. Amen.
